Review Text: HUECU is terriﬁc at most things. The staﬀ is friendly and basic services are competitive. My one problem is that I am unable to electronically transfer funds out of my Cambridge-based account to my other bank. I have reported the problem and had no resolution in 5--going on 6--weeks. They have the ticket in the system requesting resolution of the problem, but NO ONE HAS. :-(

It is unfortunate that a credit union bearing Harvard's name has such low quality customer service and credit card services. When their service representatives can't resolve an issue, they often resort to "someone will get back to you in 1-2 business days." I've had this happen to me several times and I have sometimes missed callbacks (other times I'm not sure if they actually called me back). This is very inconvenient and frustrating and should not be part of their standard business operation. Recently, I did a balance transfer online after speaking with a person on the phone to conﬁrm the terms for balance transferring. When I received my statement two weeks later, I saw that they charged me additional interest on top of the transfer fee. They categorized the transfer as a "cash advance" and they are charging me the high monthly interest. When I called in, they agreed with me that this was an error but they could not resolve the issue. They, instead, directed me to their Member Services Dept and I was told that they would get back to me in 1-2 days... I would not recommend this card. Their customer service department is unpleasant to deal with. Their website is clunky... If they are serious about enhancing their company (as it seems they are trying to do from their eﬀorts via newsletters and revamping their website), they need to focus on quality customer service and make having this alumni credit card meaningful and beneﬁcial.

I am having the same issue that another alum seemed to have: my request for a balance transfer was processed as a cash advance, and now they're charging me an outrageous interest rate every month, instead of the 0% APR I was promised over the phone. Calling customer service -- either "Cardholder Services" OR "Member Services" -- results in a loop of inﬁnite runaround and promises of callbacks "within 1-2 business days"... that just never happen. Very disappinted !

I have been a member for the last two decades or so and recently switched to electronic statement delivery. I received an email about a new statement, but there is none. Moreover, the app is clunky, and the website has more functions, but it is very non-intuitive.

compare to 15 years ago, the service is getting worst. Lately, they are sending me e-Statements with their ads ( new products , photos of new hires and awards ..) on them but no images of checks that cleared the checking account. Other world they care about the business and serving you. Whoever came up with with that idea and who approved it should ﬁred.

I'm a brand new member and my experience has just been really bad so far. No one seems to be able to help me without me giving them my member number, DOB, and last four of my social security; I don't know about the rest of the world but I work in an oﬃce where I'd rather not constantly have to spill my private info, especially because I've had to call HFCU quite a few times now for various problems! Right now I'm asking how to turn oﬀ the constant notiﬁcations for every purchase and the representative had to put me on hold so they could ﬁnd out. Train your people better, please, and maybe a better method of veriﬁcation than me having to announce the last four of my SSN all the time?

If possible I would give no stars to the Harvard Federal credit Union. I have been a member of this credit union for 42 years. They recently sent out an email informing members they were updating their credit card app. I followed their instructions to update the app. That's where the problems began. I was not able to log into the new credit card app. For a short time I was able to log into the old credit card app but eventually I lost all access to the cc app. I communicated with 4 credit Union staﬀ before I ﬁnally asked to speak with a supervisor on Sept 4th. I called today to get an update and the problem is still being worked on by the 3rd party company that oversees the app. They have no timeline for when this will be resolved. If I were you I would look elsewhere for a credit union because Harvard Federal credit Union is not a reliable ﬁnancial institution. Update to my initial review: I contacted Emilio the business manager and he was able to have the problem investigated. Today he put in contact with Christopher at the credit union who helped me resolve the problem.

Reviewer Location: Upper West Side, New York, NY
Review Text: •              Updated review OK as an update to my last review, now I am terriﬁed. I called the 617 number on the Harvard FCU website due to an urgent matter (which I will explain shortly). It sounds like a generic call center who wanted all my information. I asked them for Erika the woman with whom I was working online. They did not know Erika. I asked them who they were; they said "an extension of your ﬁnancial institution." I feel like this is a house of fraud! It makes me feel icky that I gave them any information. Now the reason I was trying to get Erika on the phone is that she was FedExing me a new replacement card for previous fraud, yet the FedEx never arrived because she messed up my city and state. This place is alarming and a total mess.

This credit union is just not worth joining. Terrible customer service (eg, "someone will contact you within 1 to 2 business days" - hello, I'm calling on a business day - is there absolutely no one there to take a call from a customer? Are they all in exams or writing papers now?? I was willing to wait for someone to take my call, but the person on the phone just kept repeating the same line over and over again. I already have an account with another, better staﬀed, credit union, so why go through the aggravation of being part of a credit union that clearly does not value their customers enough to staﬀ it properly?

Harvard University Employees Credit Union (HUECU) provides exceptional service! I primarily use it for "Harvard Alumni Card" credit card! I ﬁnd the phone support and support via messaging to be prompt and greatly helpful. I use two apps - HUECU main app and also the app speciﬁcally for "Harvard Alumni Card". Both apps have excellent user interface. Only improvement I see is that the credit card transactions sometimes lag in showing in the apps. I like the cash rewards redemption of the credit card. I charge all my expenses (except rent and two utilities) to the credit card. I get a year-end summary by mail, classifying my charges in categories, which I greatly like. It would be helpful to have it in PDF form also. Overall, I ﬁnd the credit card to be enormously useful for my every day purchases and auto-pay deductions. I think it will beneﬁt people to apply for and use this credit card. Thank you for reading this review!

Horrid horrid horrid!! Don't know if it's due to incompetency or lack of care. I won't bore you with the details but it took a month for them to send me a credit card after mine was shut down due to fraudulent activity. They sent me a card with the wrong expiration so I couldn't order anything online over the holidays. Chris Robledo gave me his email and told me that he would follow up but he never did and I couldn't reach him when I called. They kept saying they were concerned and someone named Emilio would call me to follow up but that didn't happen either. I have been with the Harvard Credit Union for well over 10 years and I don't take bad reviews lightly. Mistakes can be made but the way they handled it was egregious.

I had to read some of the 1 star reviews, because I have NEVER had a one star episode with HUECU in my 25 year history with them. I ﬁnd them to be accessible, polite, helpful, considerate, and have helped me when no other institutions would. I am not saying they are perfect, or their ﬁrst attempts at online banking were without limitations, but in comparison to alternatives like BofA or Citibank, I can actually talk to a person in under 5 minutes. That alone gets them 3 stars every time because I am in California. Thank the universe for HUECU! I'm so happy to have them in my corner!

I'm very happy with Harvard FCU. I've used them for many years for personal banking and lending for my home. I've always experienced excellent customer service and their products are very competitive.

I have been a member for more than 20 years. HUECU is the best. The oﬃcers and staﬀ are eﬃcient & very knowledgeable. I always get my questions answered & info requested immediately. They have good cd rate specials. I trust HUECU and recommend them without hesitation.

This card will likely not work if you travel overseas. I set up a travel alert for the card, went to Spain, made a half dozen charges with no issues, and then suddenly all charges were declined. I contacted Harvard card's fraud line and they cleared the hold on the card. The next charge after they said it was good to use was also declined. I called again to verify the charge was valid, and the hold was cleared. 30 minutes later another small charge was also declined. The card is useless for international travel and they left me in a bind to use debit cards.
I joined the CU as an active worker and I am with them in retirement oversea. They continue to serve my needs.

Detelina Markova was great. She has not only provided exemplary customer service, but also anticipated other needs and products I might need. I have been a member for many years, but her recommendations and knowledgeable advice brought the most value to me.

Hey HEY! Harvard University Employees Credit Union (HUECU) - has been great for me, and my family. Checking, savings, mortgage and a variety of other banking services including a very easy and eﬀective set of on-line banking I'm a BIG fan - HIGHLY recommend!

I have been an employee at Boston Children's hospital for 5 years and never knew this credit union existed. My colleague suggested it to me and said there is a Longwood medical branch. I ﬁgured I'd join so I could have access to my money throughout the work week since it's so close to me. I went in there on my lunch hour around 1 and there were only 2 employees, The employee behind the teller line, a tall girl with long braids, asked me if I could come back in an hour as no one would be able to open my account until then. I questioned why the woman in the oﬃce couldn't do it and was told she was in a meeting. I asked her if she could do it and she said she had to mandate the teller line. This business was dead I was the only one in there. The whole time she was speaking to me she had her cell phone in one hand and was chewing gum so loud and rudely, I could hardly understand her. I asked if I could do it online and she said "you can try" with a slight eye roll as if I was wasting her time. There was nothing friendly about this girl and I felt as if I was annoying her. I left and I won't be back. This bank needs some nicer staﬀ if they want more business .

I have been a member for over 25 years, I wanted to change the payment date for my credit card from the 23rd date to the 30 and was told they don't do that for customers. I am planning to pay oﬀ my balance and use a bank which works with customers. It is very disheartening. Maybe they just don't care. Karen

While the Harvard Square branch location may have changed over the years, I have had a consistently fabulous experience, with the customer-facing, retail side of the Harvard Square branch of HUECU, and the credit union's telepone and web technology. I am a happy Harvard University Employees Credit Union member of 15 years, and have enjoyed similar, favorable experiences at the Harvard Square and Massachusetts General Hospital HUECU branches.

This credit union participates in the Coop Network shared branching program, nominally. The "native" member experience may be diﬀerent than mine, me being a member of a diﬀerent credit union, but I'm not sure. If not, pity the member who wants to get any actual banking done here. My story: My dad is the beneﬁciary of an insurance policy, of which my brother and I were co- holders. Dad opened the policy about 15 years ago, when he retired. I needed to cash a payout as quickly as possible, to pay a bill. The insurer wrote the check to both of us. By my CU's policy, it's too large to deposit remotely. So I tried to deposit it here. They refused to accept it, even with my brother's endorsement, even with him present. They'd only accept it, the teller said, if the account were in both our names. As if I'm going to open a joint account with my brother just because we have to cash out an insurance plan our dad opened in our names when we were barely out of high school. I was able to deposit the check problem-free at Somerville FCU, another shared branching participant. Once my own CU cleared the check, I needed to withdraw the money in a cashier's check. This branch is convenient, so I gave it another try. Not only won't they print a check of more than $1000, but they won't let anyone but you be they payee. Who the heck is that supposed to help, making checks out to oneself? Pretty esoteric use case, that. Again, no such problem at Somerville. This institution seems to go out of its way to not provide any useful services you can't already execute at an ATM -- at least to shared branching customers. They might as well drop out of the program.

I've been a member for over 10 years since graduating from Harvard. This is not the card to get. The website never remembers your browser so you have to go through an elaborate registration program EVERY time you log into your account on the SAME computer with the SAME IP even after you click remember me. The web interface is convoluted. If you want to access your account there are a million ways to get to it, but only ONE of those ways actually allows you to make any changes or update it. Weirdly enough the interface doesn't specify when you are at the right list of menus that allows you to access certain features. It was only through a lot of trial and error that I managed to get that squared away. When I was charged a late penalty for not clearing my $32 balance on the card (which is still aﬀected my FICO score) I requested autopay. After going through a series of menus with no end in sight. I called them. I had to ﬁllout a form and provide pictures of my ID. I sent it to them. No autopay feature was added. When I wanted to add another person to my card.After going through a series of menus with no end in sight. I called them. I had to ﬁllout a form and provide pictures IDs. I sent it to them. No additional user was added. My 8th grader can design a better security feature, UI, customer service portal, and online forms than their website. Who the hell works there? How did Harvard give its name to this horrible bank?

I hate leaving bad reviews and I am happy to change this to something positive. Richard L. was able to explain the reason this happened and what they are doing to prevent it in the future. While my other cards have caught fraud more quickly, when there has been a bigger issue, they were not as quick to react and reach out. Thank you to Richard for his help and I look forward to seeing the ways fraud prevention and reporting are improved for this card :)

Like many other reviewers, I have had a bad experience with their mortgage department. The communication is so poor. You can tell the employee would just copy and paste text into his emails but then wouldn't even re-read what he was pasting. He would write emails that were totally incorrect with incorrect instructions ... i.e. please send me a copy of your condo-owners agreement .... I am not buying a condo!. This made the process so confusing. Also agree with other reviewers that their online banking system is so confusing and poorly designed. Save yourself the hassle and go someplace else.

They charged my account $20 a month for over a year without even trying to contact me to let me know. Once I found out they had been counting down my account like leeches I closed the account right away. Also when I closed it and asked for a check they did not ask for any ID, I just emailed with a signature and gave them an address. How secure is that? Peace.

I had my mortgage with BofA, but HUECU had a lower interest rate and I went with it, BIG MISTAKE!!!!!. people in the mortgage department are making mistakes left and right and do not appologize for these mistakes. I got a very diﬃcult to understand letter, I was not sure if I had to add $30, $483 or $567.79 to my escrow account, so I called customer service, spoke to Loral and she gave me the email address of Flo Colarossi and Jayne Matthews, I sent an email to them asking which was is it? and why last year analysis ended in a deﬁcit of $196.65, it was obvious that last year the analysis was wrong, could this analysis be wrong as well? long story short I got an email back from Jayne Matthews telling me: "Sonia, Per your request should you not want to have your monthly payment increase, then you can deposit monies into your escrow account. The amount would be $1,286.80." No good morning, no we are sorry we screwed up again. I was complaining that I had to add $567.79 to my escrow account, but noooo it is now $1,286.80, no explanation as to why, no appologies, NOTHING!! I had to wait 24 hours to answer to her email so I could keep my cool. I wish I could reﬁ with another bank ASAP but I am stuck with the ineptitude of HUECU's mortgage department for now. I know HUECU does not own my loan they only manage it, I will contact the people who owns it to let them know of HUECU's lack of ability to do so. Sonia M.

I'm not one to exaggerate--honestly. But the Harvard credit union is, hands down, the worst banking institution I've ever worked with. I highly, highly recommend against opening an account with them. I've never had any BIG issues with them, but I have small issues with them on a very regular basis. They include: - incredibly narrow hours of operation - disengaged, borderline incompetent customer service - sluggish, outdated mobile app and website - the cheapest, least durable debit/credit cards i've ever seen. they're the thinnest plastic possible, and the magnetic strip lasts less than a year - did i say the hours were terrible? i lost $1,000 from my *checking* account in fraudulent charges, and they didn't even have a 24-hour phone line to take care of it. i had to wait until the next business day. 2017! The operation is so amateur that it would be funny were they not in charge of my money. I made the mistake of opening an account with them when I became aﬃliated with Harvard, and as soon as my credit card is paid oﬀ I plan on immediately closing my account. If you want a good, modern bank account in Boston go to BofA.

I've had an account and credit card with HUECU for 13 years. I'm surprised to see so many horrible reviews; I've found them to be friendly and easy to work with. I opened an account at the beginning of college and liked it so much that I kept it, even though I now live across the country. My favorite aspects have been the absence of fees and the ease of reaching a human on the phone. Representatives have been nice and helpful when I've talked to them. HUECU has also been quick to alert me the few times fraudulent charges have made on my card, and they instantly refunded those charges. My main complaints have been that certain functions - particularly AutoPay and recurring transfers - are nearly impossible to ﬁnd on the website. Not sure AutoPay settings are even available online. Also, I get charged a small fee to use the debit card at other banks' ATMs (an annoyance when you live out of state), and the limit on my credit card is still pretty low after all these years (it has gradually increased from $500 to $4000, probably because it's a student card). As a result, I recently decided to make this my backup account instead of my primary bank account. But overall, I've had a really nice experience with HUECU and plan to keep my account and card permanently. I'd rate them 3.5 stars. Since I think Yelp's average rating is quite a bit lower than they deserve, I'll round up to 4.

I've belonged to HUECU for years. They provide good services, their website and mobile banking are easy to use and you get answers from a real person when you call or email a question. Customer Service is great.

I'm writing this 2 years after I moved from Cambridge- this is how much I hate this CU. Please listen to my experiences, stay away from these people. I've had so many bad experiences. Wish I could give zero stars. The staﬀ is extremely rude and unprofessional. When I went to an appointment to inquire about a mortgage loan, the guy was actually ANGRY that I was thinking about buying a house and almost brought me to tears. I've had trouble multiple times withdrawing MY money from MY checking account, where I had to basically insist that this was possible and for them to ﬁnd a way to do it, because some staﬀ were not aware of the procedures and treated me like a criminal (just because it was a larger amount I was trying to transfer out). Even though I moved away 2 years ago and stopped using this CU, I somehow still end up getting shafted by them to this day. Somehow I had a $50 charge on my credit card there that I completely forgot about- they almost sent me to collections after claiming they contacted me about payment multiple times, which never happened.

I haven't written a review in a long time, but I felt like this bank..excuse me credit union needed one. In one word: terrible. I didn't think an establishment would be able to stress me out, but they did it. I received the privilege to sign up for HUECU from being an employee of a Harvard company. The ﬁrst thing I noticed were the terrible hours, hard to get to locations. Then their online presence is weak, customer service horrid AND you get charged for breathing. There are no beneﬁts of joining this bank. Go elsewhere.

My husband and I moved our ﬁnances from Bank of America to HUECU about ﬁve years ago and we could not be happier with our decision. HUECU oﬀers all the beneﬁts and convenience (and then some) of a large commercial bank. I am so appreciative of their incredible customer service, user- friendly online platform and mobile banking app, fraud protection/alerts, etc. etc. I can also speak to their mortgage lending program: We are in the process of applying for our second home loan with them. First time we worked with Daisy Familia, who was great. Currently we are working with Sharon Cummings who has exceeded all our expectations with her vast knowledge, clear communication, time invested in us, and so forth. I would not imagine going anywhere else.

I have been a customer for over seven years; HUECU has been my ﬁnancial institution. After a recent major medical emergency that resulted in a long hospitalization and has upended my life, I called to inquire about ﬁnancial hardship assistance, as advertised on their website. The agent I spoke with instead made unkind comments in reference to my illness, resulting disability, and speciﬁc recent purchases with my debit card and also repeatedly suggested that HUECU was not my main ﬁnancial institution and that I should be working things out with another bank or credit union.

Rarely do I have to endure such rude customer service reps. I recently signed up for an alumni Mastercard. On two occasions, I called customer service, and on both occasions, the rep I spoke with was a total jerk. On neither occasion was I calling with a complaint -- No. Rather, I was calling with a simple, basic question about my MasterCard, and by 'simple' I mean this: "Are there foreign transaction fees?" Quick-&-easy question, politely asked. Any professional rep would have ﬁred oﬀ the right answer and then hustled me oﬀ the phone in a jiﬀy. But not these people. Both conversations lasted twice as long as they needed to because I had to listen to the snide. Apparently, they're doing me a big favor by taking my call. They'd be downright comical if they weren't so downright grating. Eek Lifehack: If you're in a very good mood and wish to quickly transition into a very bad one -- just call HUECU customer service!! Works like a charm, every time.

Terrible service, terrible communication. Never answered my questions. I've had an account with them for three years and it's disappointing to be treated so poorly. If I wanted terrible service and no communication I'd bank with BOA. I do not recommend and will be withdrawing my business from them.

I've been a member for two years now and recently stumbled on them on yelp. Wow, such terrible reviews. I've only interacted with the staﬀ over email and the online messaging system, but everything has been prompt and correct. I utilize checking, money market savings, and a couple CDs with competitive rates. So far so good.

It is simply just not a good bank. They are slow, they don't communicate well, and have made every interaction with them unnecessarily painful. They are also very outdated in terms of technology. deﬁnitely the worst credit union I have ever used, and I would not recommend it to a friend.

We have had an amazing experience working with HUECU for the mortgage on our ﬁrst home. Daisy Familia has been absolutely wonderful: friendly, knowledgeable, responsive. Daisy and the underwriting team worked through our application very quickly and we were able to close within 3 weeks of signing the Purchase and Sale agreement. The closing costs and mortgage rate were also far better compared to other lenders. Altogether, I can wholeheartedly recommend HUECU.

From day to day op's, to the fraud department, to the loan department, this institution aﬃrms why credit unions are so elite. Special shout out to Iris in the loan department for her exceptional customer service, subject matter specialty and professionalism. She truly went above and beyond in assisting me and I'm forever grateful. Much love HUECU..

"I will always be grateful to HUECU as you have been there for me during the most challenging ebbs and ﬂows of my life. I joined HUECU very soon after graduating medical school at the beginning of my internship at MGH. You continue to have a branch right in the hospital and it made it so easy for me as a busy intern. I secured my ﬁrst car loan with the help of my Dad and felt so proud to be aﬃliated with your credit union. You saw me through residency, fellowship, marriage, the purchase of my ﬁrst home, the birth of my two children, a terrible ﬁnancially devastating divorce, and my ﬁrst home post divorce (you carried the home loan). You have these wonderful ﬁnancial seminars and I was so grateful to have my two teenage children start HUECU checking and savings accounts. Now as I build my forever home with the help of yet another HUECU home loan, I am humbled with gratitude for the tremendous support of MY amazing HUECU. So, I am now a lifetime member as are my two children. As they both head oﬀ to college this fall, I am feel so secure in knowing that they have the support of HUECU should they need it. It has not been easy being a single home and HUECU has been there with me every step of the way. Thank you HUECU for being there for us during the ﬁnancial good times and the bad. I look forward to starting savings accounts for my furniture grandchildren one day. Happy Birthday! Here's to 82 more years!"

Granted, there was a bit of a wait, but it is what to expect that, arriving at a busy bank in a busy part of town on a busy day. However, there is ample seating, free coﬀee, and entertainment to watch in the interim if I hadn't some paperwork to ﬁll in for my new account. I walked away within the hour with a savings and a checkings account, and my new debit card, I was able to set up online banking the very same day and use my debit card the next day. I can also use Apple Pay/NFC payments and link the account to my existing bank account. HUECU oﬀers free banking and depending on your usage at least ten out-of-network ATM transaction fees are waived each month with an additional reimbursement as well. Service was pleasant, thorough and I felt like I was well informed and given the time to discuss my options.

The credit card has worked well for me, particularly as a card to use abroad. While I have had a bit of trouble with their website, they have been responsive in getting me through the problem and they appear to be designing an upgrade to make it more intuitive.

Ok, I think I see where these mixed reviews are coming from. I have been a customer here for 15 years or so. For the most part it's just their day to day operations which I've had good luck with. They have always been professional and courteous with me. Once, when my card had been compromised, they held my new card at a close branch and kept open a couple of extra minutes so that I wouldn't be without access to money. On the other hand, my loan transfer and reﬁ were about 15 years ago and it sounds like it was a diﬀerent bank back then. The only familiar problem I had with some of the other reviewers was when I had applied for a home equity loan a year ago. I was dragged along and one person said I was all set and then another woman said that I wouldn't get it when I had three times that in retirement and had never been late on a payment. I was very surprised at that. I also talked to a woman about a loan prior to applying who was never in and it took half a dozen phone calls before I got my questions answered. So, sounds like the credit union is great for day to day bank account, credit card (which has been great for me and the best rate going), etc. but loans, mortgage, etc. not so much.

I am giving one star (zero if I could) to the incompetent way they handle foreign transactions of my Harvard Alumni Mastercard. I have been a card holder for well over 10 years. Usually I rely on this card to shop while abroad since there is no foreign transaction fee. I just came back from 2 weeks in Eastern Europe. During these two weeks I had to call these people 6 times - yes, 6! - because my card kept getting blocked. I put a travel notice on the account and yet it kept being blocked and no one at this HUECU card member services could do anything other than to express how sorry they are. I was given the same constant run around - called card member services to be veriﬁed, transferred to card member security to be re-werifed, card unblocked, next day card gets blocked again. Frustrating beyond belief, not to mention the expense and hassle of calling international, wasting time on my vacation, and the constant stress of not knowing whether or not I can check out of a store with purchases. HUECU must have a better way to address such situation - if their algorithm repeatedly ﬂags transactions and member already put a travel notice and already called, ﬁnd a better algorithm, do manual override, so something! Their claim to be "not just a bank but a beneﬁt" is a joke.

•                 Updated review Harvard University Employees Credit Union is a great place to bank, oﬀering convenient locations and beneﬁts for their members other banks do not oﬀer. I have never found the staﬀ unfriendly or in any way rude, either on the phone or in person - I would say quite the opposite and customer service reps always try to help resolve the issue - whatever it may be.

In all the years I have been banking I have never experienced such poor customer service and impersonal banking. I have a savings account with this bank because it's an aﬃliate of my place of employment. I decided to do a student loan reﬁnance with them and let's just say we are going on two weeks and I have made multiple phone calls to them to verify my documents so I can ﬁnish my loan process. I have called 5 diﬀerent times and each time I keep getting told that my documents have been reviewed and I'm all set then I get a text telling me they have been rejected and I have to upload new documents and call back again and go through the whole process. On two occasions the lender had exactly what they needed the underwriter just didn't look at all three pages uploaded. This whole thing has been a complete waste of time and I am still not done yet! If I hadn't taken the hit on my credit score I would tell the bank to go kick rocks and I would go to a diﬀerent lender. This is ridiculous! I went to the physical bank to resolve my issue and they referred me to their website and sat with me while I made yet another phone call. Useless! What's the point in having a banker when they can't even manage a loan?!

I have been trying to apply for a personal loan which was approved but now struggling with closing the loan. They do not give a list of documents instead everyday I need to upload something new or ﬁll in a new form. Worst experience I have ever had with a bank. The Customer Care people are not helpful. It is so frustrating having to make calls and being put on hold for 15 min only to be told I need to upload a document that is already in their system. Such incompetence is extremely spectacular.
I've been a member for 2 years. Aﬀordable checking, good loan rates and most importantly very pleasant people.

Oh my goodness. worst bank ever. Staﬀ not courteous. wait time is long - only 2 of their 4 counters are opened on a Friday afternoon (which is obviously a busy time). Bad service. I so want to love this credit union but despite being a member for 11 years, I cannot. Everyone who works here is incredibly nice but competence is a trait that seems to be sorely lacking. Exhibit A: I wanted to do an international electronic transfer from this credit union to a credit union in Ontario. Easy-peasy, right? I mean, it is 2018 and e-transfers happen globally every second of the day. Wrong! It took literally 30 days and untold hours on my part calling and checking in, corralling the Harvard CU troops, to try and try again before the transfer went through. And once it did, no one could tell me why it took so long in order to preclude a similar disaster if I was stupid enough to attempt a similar transaction through them again. I could/should have given up after a week but I was so incensed and determined to see the transaction through that I couldn't give up until they ﬁgured it out and pushed it through. I could have walked to Ontario and delivered the money more quickly than going through this credit union. Next time. Exhibit B: I applied for and was approved for a HELOC. Right before the closing, I emailed the loan oﬃcer to be sure that everything was in place, that I didn't need to bring anything to the closing, and they didn't need any further paperwork from me. I was assured everything was all set. A month after the closing, I got an email from someone else telling me they hadn't received the insurance binder and needed one. Called the insurance company and was told they had sent it. Now, seven months later, I got a call again from the CU telling me audit reveals they still claim not to have the insurance binder. Called my insurance company again and they forwarded to me the insurance binder that had been emailed to the credit union last March. This credit union is a complete disaster. I still use them for a savings account but go to a real bank for important transactions. The tellers seem to be the most competent people in the place.

I have been a loyal Harvard alum for 50 years and have used many of its aﬃliated services, but my experience with HUECU and its Alumni Master Card program is the worst banking relationship I have had in a ﬁnance and investment career. Let's start with the website and online banking. The website purports to oﬀer online banking services similar to other ﬁnancial institutions like eStatements and past statement history. Yet I discovered after many failed attempts and ﬁnally talking to the third- party company that provides the online banking software, that some institutions do not provision some of the bank end services. So despite saying that one can get a history of transactions online (doesn't work for more than two most recent periods), a supervisor (Nick) told me he would have to request the past statement history from MC and then he sent by USPS the printed versions of the PDFs to me over a week later. More frustrating is that with online accounting software like Quicken or Quickbooks -- which have been around for decades -- one cannot download transactions from HUECU in a format to import into these programs. I was told that I would have to enter the transactions manually (!!). The frustration of having no clue that certain functionality doesn't work is enormous, but more importantly, there are actual and implied representations regarding the online banking service which are deceptive, if not potentially fraudulent, even if unintentional. I should also note that I sent emails and hard copy of emails to executives of the CU but never received a conﬁrmation or reply. I also agree with the other reviews about incompetence and laziness. I submitted a form in late June 2017 via the website (customer service requested this method) requesting that my account be closed and card cancelled. Ironically, I received subsequent call from Nick who wanted to know my reasons for doing so. I told him, and reminded him that he had talked to me over a year earlier. He said he would take care of it. Last night (7/26/17) I logged onto the HUECU site to check the account. I had not received any conﬁrmation of the account being closed. To my surprise, I had a $25 balance. So I called this morning and was told that the $25 charge had posted in mid-July despite my request that the account be closed. Moreover when I asked the the customer service rep to look at the notes in the account, he told me he did not have access to the communication I had with HUECU about closing the account. I read him the riot act and he then, meekly, found communciation acknowledging my request in a "sorry to see you go" email from one of his associates. This organization is more than incompetent. Employees seem entitled with no ambition to provide a real service. Be warned. Especially about the Alumni MC.
